newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended ahead but well off their day's highs on Monday after fading into the close as strong U.S. industrial output figures spiked a promising rally, dealers said.
With volumes still low ahead of year-end book closings, players remained nervous about the risk of big swings, one broker said, and the market was still closely tracking the German Bund future.
"We are running on empty at the moment, whether things are moving up or down," he said. Interest was unlikely to pick up before the new year, he added.

The market was lifted early by benign German business confidence data, extending gains through the midsession, but the largest rise in U.S. industrial output for nine months rapidly reawakened inflation fears and drove prices lower.
November output rose 0.9 percent, well above a forecast 0.6 percent jump.

Dutch bonds still managed to outperform Bunds handily, with the ten year yield discount widening to eight basis points from six on Friday. The spread on the long bond moved out to around 22 basis points from 19 last week. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
